history.period: 1893; Ganesh festival origins traced to 1893, temple idol traditions from 1896-1897
history.summary: Founded in 1893 by Dagdusheth Halwai, a wealthy Pune sweet-seller, and his wife Lakshmibai after they lost their son(s) to a plague epidemic; their guru Madhavnath Maharaj advised them to build the shrine. The first eco-friendly idol was crafted by sculptor Shri Naik, and Dagdusheth was among the hosts Lokmanya Tilak drew into the public ten-day Ganesh Utsav of 1893. After the 1896 plague deaths, Dagdusheth's widow had a second Ganesha idol made by Shri Naik, which young people began celebrating as a public festival in 1897. The Shreemant Dagdusheth Halwai Sarvajanik Ganpati Trust today runs extensive philanthropy, including an old-age home and schooling for destitute children at Kondhwa. The 2.2-metre idol is adorned with nearly 40 kg of gold, guarded by marble sentinels Jay and Vijay.

name: Dagdusheth Halwai Ganpati Temple
town_description: Pune is Maharashtra's second-largest city and the former seat of the Maratha Peshwas, often called the state's cultural capital and the 'Oxford of the East' for its many universities and research institutes. It is today a major IT, automotive and manufacturing hub. Its old-city core around Shaniwar Wada, the Peshwa-era temples and the Parvati hill is dense with historic and religious landmarks.

travel.road: Central Budhwar Peth, near Appa Balwant Chowk and Shaniwar Wada; reachable by city buses, auto-rickshaws and cabs from all parts of Pune
